trust_decision.summary: Whether registry credentials (Authorization header, or credentials resolved for the original host) may go to an HTTP origin other than the one the caller targeted; decided in auth.Client.send (redirect following delegated to net/http, which strips Authorization only on hostname change) and in auth.Client.Do after a 401 (credentials resolved for originalReq.Host and replayed regardless of which origin issued the challenge).

landing_point.why: The summary says 'forwards credentials across redirects'; the only place redirects are followed is c.client().Do in send, so an engineer adds a CheckRedirect there first.

fix_sites.entry_point: auth.Client.Do (and every remote.Repository/remote.Registry operation through Repository.do / Registry.do; also token fetches via fetchDistributionToken / fetchOAuth2Token)
fix_sites.module_kind: auth-decorated HTTP client, send helper (redirect policy)

fix_sites.entry_point: auth.Client.Do with a hand-built *http.Request whose Host field is empty
auth.Client.Do when the 401 challenge is returned by a redirected-to origin (pre-auth redirect)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All three fix sites are in registry/remote/auth/client.go; the pre-auth challenge-origin check (fix.diff:79-81) is the least obvious but it is in the same function the landing point leads to.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the OAuth2 password-grant body (registry/remote/auth/client.go:412-441): 'the advisory is about the Authorization header and registry redirects; this is the token service, the secret sits in a form body, and replaying a 307 body is standard net/http behaviour'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Credentials must still be forwarded across same-origin redirects (path-only redirect, default-port normalisation example.com == example.com:443, case-insensitive host), and a caller-supplied http.Client.CheckRedirect must still be invoked; cross-host bearer realms (auth.docker.io) and docker.io -> registry-1.docker.io must keep working.

O6_input_shapes: redirect to different port on same host
default port explicit vs implicit (normalised equal)
redirect after auth (Authorization already set) vs redirect before auth (401 issued by redirect target)
request with empty req.Host (falls back to URL.Host)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: OAuth2 password/refresh-token grant POSTs credentials in a form body; on a 307/308 from the token endpoint net/http replays the body to the new origin, and the fix's CheckRedirect only deletes the Authorization header.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Token service rather than registry; credential is in the body, not a header; advisory and tests talk only about the Authorization header.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, different function (fetchOAuth2Token), reached only when Credential has RefreshToken or ForceAttemptOAuth2 is set

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Blob upload PUT copies Authorization from resp.Request (the post-redirect POST); a variant that copies it from the original req, or skips the sameUploadHost check for a redirected POST, re-forwards credentials cross-origin.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The 'reuse credential from previous POST request' comment already shows the maintainers manually propagating auth outside auth.Client.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Range re-request clones the stored request; a variant storing resp.Request (post-redirect URL with copied Authorization) would bypass auth.Client's origin logic.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Seek-by-new-connection lives in an internal package far from auth; a maintainer optimising to skip the redirect hop would plausibly store the final request.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Pagination Link resolved against resp.Request.URL; a variant that attaches the previous page's Authorization to the next-page request would leak across origins.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Pagination code already reads the redirected request; carrying auth along to save a 401 round-trip is a plausible optimisation.

O9_family: credential forwarding to an unintended origin across HTTP redirects (CWE-200/CWE-522)

O10_build.project_tests: registry/remote/auth/client_test.go (httptest servers, offline); registry/remote/repository_test.go for upload Location checks

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a CheckRedirect in send that strips Authorization on host change only (or on any redirect), missing the port/scheme case, the pre-auth 401-from-redirect-target path in Do, and breaking same-origin redirects or a caller's CheckRedirect.

out_of_scope_notes: registry/remote/repository.go:880 sameUploadHost compares Hostname() case-sensitively (fails closed, not a leak).
Headers from auth.Client.Header (registry/remote/auth/client.go:137-139) are forwarded across redirects; only matters if a caller puts secrets there.
